summary: This is a sound, rules-clean restack of decode's own neutral fused-preattention-triton onto the current master (1.1665x). It adds attention master's PAIRED in-kernel pad, so 5 launches become 1 on every shape. Expect about +0.8-1.2% on the headline, inside the CI, so judge it per shape on the batch-1 rows. Dispatch it only after paired-heads-pad-unpad-triton (job a92b64be4c6547d3) has harvested, and fix the conditional base before claim time. No companion is needed.
justification: Mechanism: on master kernel_fn the pre-attention step is still SGLang's FusedQKNorm, the two k/v .to(FP8) casts, the store_cache JIT and either q.view().to(FP8) (unpaired) or, once paired-heads lands, _pair_pad_q_kernel. That is five launches of a few hundred bytes to a few hundred KB each, all latency-bound. One Triton program per (token, head) at num_warps 1 is roughly 2-3 us at T<=32, so about 4-7 us is saved per shape. The same 5->1 gave muse_attention_decode 3.5-6.4 us. Profile support is indirect. In master's profile (9dcaec316b3045a7) none of the five kernels reaches the top-12 rows on any shape; they are all in the '... N more' tail (each under about 2.8 us at full decode_1). The archived profile text and JSON carry only the truncated report, so the replaced kernels' own us cannot be read from top_kernels; only the row count ('... 14 more' vs '... 21 more') and the shape totals can. The parent's per-shape rows are the best evidence: decode_1 +1.6-2.1% (sliding 172.8->167.0, full 182.1->176.8), verify_1 +0.2-1.7%, sliding decode_32 +3.3%, and everything else flat or within -1%, including full verify_32 at T=256 with 4,608 programs (0.990, no loss). Since then post-expert-norm-triton-small-t has shrunk the T<32 totals (sliding decode_1 is now 145.8 us, full 157.0 us), so the same ~4-5 us is now about 3% of those shapes. That makes the decode_1 'faster' and verify_1 'faster' directions credible. The sliding decode_32 'faster' is weakly founded: it was the parent's one out-of-drift shape, at 3.3% when the replaced launches are worth about 1.5% of 252 us there. Treat it as probably drift rather than a prediction. Full decode_16 and verify_16 'faster' on the paired path is about 1% of 365/604 us, which is inside the per-shape drift. Verify_32 'flat' is right. On the floors, every shape sits 3-4x off speed of light, dominated by Marlin, FA3 and the nvjet GEMMs, so this is launch hygiene and not a move toward SoL. Headline arithmetic: decode_1 load about +2.5-3%, verify_1 about +1.5%, the other four loads about +0.3-0.7% each, so the geomean is about +0.8-1.2%. That is below the ~1.5% CI half-width, and the result will very likely classify neutral or within-ci again. It needs promotion by hand on per-shape evidence, as the DECISIONS precedent did. Weakest link: the expected magnitude rests on launch-count arithmetic for kernels this profile cannot show. The parent's own decode_1 gain (+2%) is the same size as the drift LESSONS documents (1.5-2.5% per shape), so even the best-evidenced rows can be read either way from one run. A second, smaller weakness is that the spec tells the implementer to merge the parent's 'prepare() warm-up', but the parent patch has no warm-up; its prepare() hunk only removes qk_norm.
confounders: paired-heads-pad-unpad-triton (running, depends_on, not yet landed): the spec's base is conditional ('master if it landed, else on its branch'). If this is built on the unmerged branch, the measured delta against BEST mixes that hypothesis's own pad/unpad effect into this one on all four full batch>1 shapes. If paired-heads ends neutral and is not merged, there is no defined base at all. Fix the base at claim time: build on master after that harvest. If paired-heads did not merge, PAIRED replaces master's torch.zeros plus the two slice copies (3 launches) and the un-pad copies plus FusedRMSNormGate stay, and the paired rows are then read against paired-heads' own rows, not against BEST.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched (landed): the PAIRED write only exists because of the paired path. This is an interaction by construction, not a confounder. Reverting it would delete the PAIRED half of the change.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-t (landed): it shares no code or buffers with the pre-attention step, but it cut the T<32 totals by 10-15%, which raises this change's percentage on decode_1/verify_1 relative to the parent's run. Compare per-shape us, not the parent's percentages.

full-decode-cuda-splitkv-port and sliding-fused-triton-decode1-port (running, not landed): either can remove shapes from this code path (full decode_16/32 and sliding decode_1). The splitkv branch keeps FusedQKNorm, the casts and store_cache, and takes a contiguous FP8 q [T,16,64]. This kernel with PAIRED=False produces exactly that, so it is compatible, but the restack must route that branch through the fused kernel too, because state['qk_norm'] is deleted. The implementer must read the actual master at claim time, not the spec's if/else.

marlin-block-m-cap-16 and sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8 (landed): different areas with no shared launches. They contribute only seed-dependent Marlin drift on the totals; the per-case seeds differ between runs.
interference: No companion is warranted. An ab-revert of fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched removes the code under test. An ab-revert of post-expert-norm or the Marlin cap would only change the denominators. A control that isolates the PAIRED sub-change (in-kernel pad vs _pair_pad_q_kernel) would measure one ~2 us launch on the 16-weight full batch>1 shapes, which is far below drift, so it could not disambiguate anything. The useful split is already in the run's own shapes. The unpaired batch-1 rows (full/sliding decode_1 and verify_1) measure the 5->1 fusion without PAIRED. The paired full batch>1 rows measure it with PAIRED. Full verify_32 at T=256 is the regression canary. A loss would be attributable without a companion: it would show at full/sliding verify_32, or as a correctness failure in the cache store. A gain is ambiguous only statistically, and a companion run would not fix that. If quota is tight, fold this into a combined decode check (for example with moe-align-small-t-restack-on-master, which is also inside CI) rather than spending a scored submit on about +1%.
rules_flags: No rule break found. The cache store moves into Triton but writes the same FP8 rows at cache_loc, indexed in int64, and the cache stays FP8. q and k go fp32 -> E4M3 directly instead of fp32 -> bf16 -> E4M3; that is not coarser and is allowed. The grid and constexprs (PAIRED, G, ROPE) come from config and shapes only, and there are no host syncs. The zero half of the paired query is written on every call, so nothing is cached between calls.

Keep the k/v divide before the cast and read k_scale/v_scale as device pointers. TASK.md has a correctness case with kv_scale 0.015625 (batch 4, ctx 7000, sliding, q_len 8). FA3's k_descale/v_descale must still be passed when scaled, as the parent kept them.

Do not add a prepare() warm-up that runs on judge data or writes into state. The parent patch has no warm-up, so none should be invented. If one is added for JIT, use synthetic tensors only and cover both PAIRED and both ROPE specializations.

Triton's fp8e4nv cast saturates and torch's does not. This is harmless for normed q/k, but v is not normed: v/v_scale at kv_scale 0.015625 multiplies v by 64. The parent passed 13/13 with this exact code, so it is not a blocker; keep the parent's v path verbatim.
open_questions: Which base at claim time? Gate dispatch on paired-heads-pad-unpad-triton's harvest (job a92b64be4c6547d3) rather than building on its unmerged branch. If it is not merged, should PAIRED replace master's torch.zeros plus the two copies while the un-pad block is left alone? That is the only definition that keeps this hypothesis's scope.
The spec says to merge the parent's 'prepare() warm-up', but the parent patch has none. Confirm that the implementer should skip it.

The truncated profile report (top 12 plus '... N more') cannot show the replaced kernels. Can the harvest record the full kernel list, or at least the '... N more' count and total per shape, so the 5->1 can be confirmed as launches actually removed rather than inferred from shape totals?

With an expected headline of +0.8-1.2% inside the CI, is a scored submit worth it, or should this go into a combined decode check with the other inside-CI restacks (moe-align-small-t-restack-on-master)?

If sliding-fused-triton-decode1-port lands first, sliding decode_1 (weight 46, this change's best-evidenced shape) leaves this code path, and the remaining expected gain drops to about +0.6%. Re-estimate the priority at that point.
